Header: Locusta migratoria Makanta in Bemba language

Prevention: This is a migratory pest; and therefore it is difficult to prevent the pest problem as they immigrate from outside to your fields.
The locusts feed on a wide range of plant materials and it is difficult to reduce these food sources.
Monitoring: Inspect fields of maize, sorghum, millet, wheat, rice and sugarcane regularly for this pest during the active growth of crops (locusts do not like old ripened cereals)
Locusts usually come at the beginning of the rainy season, so look out for them.
Check on vegetative parts of the grass family for signs of the droppings by locusts, which appear green even when dry.
Look for chewed leaves by the swarms of locusts.

This will help to warn other farmers.
Equally you can get the newest information about migrations of locusts in your region from these offices.
Direct Control: Manually pick them up and kill them when still in low numbers in the field.
They can serve as human and chicken food.
Fenitrothion –based products (FENIPACK 60%EC RESPACK 600g/l; and others) as flat sprays because they are little persistent in the environment.
Restrictions: Ndola in case of invasion of locusts in your district
When using a pesticide (even a botanical home-brew), always wear protective clothing.
Follow the instructions on the product label, such as dosage, timing of application, pre-harvest interval, max number of sprays, restricted re-entry interval.
